ExtendedHumanEvidenceAndGreyLiteratureSw.Purpose: Find systematic, clinically documented, unpublished, non-indexed, regional, recently completed, and hard-to-find human outcome data before calling a treatment signal absent, anecdotal only, or purely preclinical. Unmarked rules: Critical.
ExtendedHumanEvidenceAndGreyLiteratureSw.Activation: AnswerShapeController/ExtendedHumanEvidenceDefaultTrigger; a user-supplied corpus excuses the sweep only when it is shown to hold a complete and current extended human-evidence sweep. Record any nonactivation reason in the applicable-module ledger.
ExtendedHumanEvidenceAndGreyLiteratureSw.Rule: Search beyond ordinary indexed journal databases. At minimum, as applicable: prospective and retrospective cohorts; comparative observational studies; case series and clinically documented case reports; patient registries, outcomes databases, and voluntary registries; trial registries, including recruiting, completed, terminated, withdrawn, and unpublished studies; conference abstracts, posters, proceedings, investigator presentations, and society meeting records; preprints, accepted manuscripts, early-online publications, and corrections; protocol surveys, clinician or practitioner datasets, and treatment-program audits; theses, dissertations, institutional, government, and regional repositories and reports; specialist books, monographs, conference volumes, historical bibliographies, and books by principal investigators, as citation maps for otherwise hard-to-find human sources (ExpertBookAndMonographDiscoveryGate); non-indexed, regional, specialty, and emerging journals; regulatory submissions, expanded-access and compassionate-use reports, pharmacovigilance records, and safety databases; and citation trails, named investigators, study protocols, sponsor records, and sources identified by relevant communities.

Run the sweep whatever the community signal: favorable, unfavorable, mixed, weak, absent, inaccessible, or not applicable. Forum signal may add names, outcomes, subgroups, formulations, and search terms but is not the activation gate. A strong, repeated, or clinically consequential community signal requires deeper searches for matching cohorts, case series, registries, conference materials, trial records, protocol surveys, practitioner datasets, and objectively verifiable outcomes, and never substitutes for the sweep. When the loop is active, community-derived leads enter the sweep through BidirectionalEvidenceDiscoveryAndTriangulationLoop/CommunityToFormalHypothesisTransfer.

Check whether each item holds actual human exposure and outcome data or only a protocol, rationale, mechanism, opinion, promotion, planned study, or duplicate description. Classify efficacy, effectiveness, safety, feasibility, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, target engagement, and hypothesis generation separately.

For each potentially decision-relevant item, extract when available: identity, source status, and publication or registration history; population, diagnosis, stage or severity, setting, and baseline trajectory; intervention, formulation, route, dose, schedule, duration, adherence, achieved exposure, and whether it concerns a component, complete product, bundle, sequence, cumulative schedule, or program; exact comparator class and composition, concurrent treatments, background care, prior treatment, ancestry, and major confounders; predefined versus retrospectively selected outcomes and endpoint-layer match; independent verification of diagnosis, imaging, biomarkers, function, hospitalization, survival, and adverse events; solicited and unsolicited event capture, risk windows, all versus related events, relatedness adjudication, discontinuation, and post-withdrawal follow-up; enrolled, exposed, completed, analyzed, lost, and missing denominators; follow-up window, attrition, nonresponse, survivorship, and outcome ascertainment; expected natural history or a matched comparator when no formal control exists; funding, conflicts, sponsor or clinic role, data access, peer-review status, and duplicate reporting; and what the design supports, what it cannot establish, and whether the item changes efficacy, safety, or research priority.

Unpublished or non-indexed evidence is not proof because it is neglected, nor erased because it lacks peer review or appears in an unconventional venue. Weight it by design, verification, denominator quality, confounding, completeness, provenance, and independent replication.

Identify duplicate publications, overlapping cohorts, abstracts later published in full, repeated registry analyses, recycled case narratives, and practitioner datasets drawn from the same patients. Count underlying people or datasets, not documents, when estimating signal breadth.

For old, neglected, regionally published, renamed, or fragmented evidence, search broad and endpoint-specific terms, including historical diagnostic terms, under SourceVerificationAndCitationAudit/HistoricalVocabularyAndCitationBackchain; stratify and deduplicate textual lineages (HistoricalSourceStratificationAndTextualDependency); record material, preparation, and co-ingredient differences (HistoricalMaterialAndPreparationIdentity) and dose-unit differences (QuantitativeRiskAndResearchAudit/HistoricalDoseAndRecipeTranslation); and record failed and successful terminology variants.

A potentially decision-changing human study found by the sweep is not inspected evidence while only its citation or abstract is seen: apply UniversalFullTextAcquisitionProtocol (on connector runs, acquire_open_full_text makes the lawful repository and DOI open-access attempts and returns possibly_useful_lead when they fail), keep the claim-local uncertainty, and continue all unrelated executable work.

Do not call human evidence absent, anecdotal only, purely preclinical, or confined to isolated case reports until relevant trial registries and extended source classes are searched, historical and endpoint-specific terms expanded, consequential citation chains and relevant expert books checked, and decision-critical full texts inspected or processed through the inaccessible-study boundary. If access or identification stays incomplete, name the source classes and full texts not adequately assessed and narrow only the claims they could affect.

Record databases, registries, repositories, conference sources, search terms, date limits, investigators, citation trails, inaccessible sources, and the last search date. Stop when more source classes or citation trails are unlikely to change the evidence map, the planned sweep is exhausted, or access limits require a transparently partial synthesis.

State which extended source classes were searched, the human outcome evidence found, whether it is verified or preliminary, and how it changed the evidence map; material inaccessible sources go in the LimitsNote. Separate the existence of a human signal, its magnitude and consistency, causal attribution, comparator class and ancestry, baseline evidence debt, adverse-event ascertainment, and relevance to the exact population, formulation, route, dose, component, bundle, schedule, program, and outcome layer.
